Tiszadada Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tiszadada, Hungary

Not demolished. This is the older of two Jewish cemeteries in Tiszadada. Tradition holds that Jews first arrived in the second half of the 18th century and founded a burial society in 1800, though an 1840 census oddly records no Jewish inhabitants at all - a discrepancy the sources don't resolve. By a later census, the Orthodox community numbered 231 (9.4% of the village), later declining to 164 by 1920 and 157 by 1941. The community built its first synagogue in 1901, designed by Károly Kiss, and Tiszadada was also home to Hasidic followers of the Munkacser Rebbe, Rabbi Spira Hajim Elazar, who maintained a separate synagogue using Sephardic nusach. A noted local rabbi, Jehoshua Brisk, had studied under the 'Wonder Rabbi' of Liszka. In late April 1944, Tiszadada's Jews were gathered in the synagogue garden and robbed by Hungarian gendarmerie before being deported via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz; only 14 returned in 1949, and the community was never re-established. The synagogue was later demolished, though a fragment of its Ten Commandments tablet survives in a local museum. Based on tombstone dating, this older cemetery ceased use around 1938, after which burials moved to Tiszadada's newer cemetery.
